Q: Question about planning prior to making a website A:

I'm trained in project management surrounding website design. I've been in this for around 15+ years, I'll explain a step-by-step tutorial on how to effectively get your plans across to the client, I'll try to use as little abbreviations so you can understand.

I would personally suggest incorporating the following subjects for your plans:

How to form your proposal

  1. Empathy map

  2. User story (As a..., I want..., So that..., GIVE SOLUTION FOR USER'S NEED)

  3. Give descriptions on system functions like performance, security, usability, reliability and scalability (NFR)

  4. Explain the processes and functions of the website (outline logical code that you'd use with Javascript, Basically... FR)

  5. Decomposition of each web page

  6. Key Performance Indicators for the website and business (website: bounce rate, loading times, avg time on page business: % of repeated visitors, % of satisfied visitors.

  7. Outline features of the website

  8. Justify your reasoning for these plans

  9. discuss in different sections (How it meets the client's needs, Risk mitigation, Laws and legislation)

Website design documentation

  1. Logo, colors and any images

  2. The pages and their description with images

  3. Data dictionary: Column names, defining Data Type, Special characteristics of columns like NOT NULL or UNIQUE.

  4. ERD diagram, Level 0 and level 1 DFD diagram... level 0 is a system that connects with external entities like users. but a level 1 DFD contains categories like users (employee, customer, etc), processes (Set-up account, withdraw cash, etc), and databases (users_info, orders, etc). RESEARCH GANE-SARSON DFD.

  5. How each page connects up

  6. Flowcharts for any functions in the website

  7. Wireframes of each page

  8. How you'd test the website for the future

  9. A conclusion with everything outlined

I hope this helps, I wish you your best on this journey into designing and planning websites.

Q: Android Studio Emulator keeps exiting with error 139 on ubuntu 24.04 A:

There are two physical GPU, while it is unclear which -gpu option is being passed.

emuglConfig_init: vulkan_mode_selected:host gles_mode_selected:host

emuglConfig_get_vulkan_hardware_gpu_support_info: Found physical GPU 'NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2070 with Max-Q Design', type: VK_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_TYPE_DISCRETE_GPU, apiVersion: 1.4.325, driverVersion: 590.48
emuglConfig_get_vulkan_hardware_gpu_support_info: Found physical GPU 'Intel(R) UHD Graphics (CML GT2)', type: VK_PHYSICAL_DEVICE_TYPE_INTEGRATED_GPU, apiVersion: 1.4.318, driverVersion: 25.2.8

Initializing VkEmulation features:
   glInteropSupported: false

The command line is the first line, which has no special options ...

emulator -netdelay none -netspeed full -avd Medium_Phone_API_36.1 -qt-hide-window -grpc-use-token -idle-grpc-timeout 300

To debug, add options -gpu, -verbose, or -show-kernel. Or try to disable Vulkan -feature -Vulkan. There's no way to tell which GPU to use. One GPU being present is being assumed.

I don't know what "UHD Graphics (CML GT2)" means, but the UHD 620 has known issues with Vulkan: Emulator Not Starting-up in Android Studio: The emulator process for AVD has terminated

Intel's Comet Lake GT2 GPU is probably something alike UHD 630.

Just see Troubleshoot known issues with Android Emulator

  • If your machine has both an Intel GPU and a discrete GPU, disable the Intel GPU in Device Manager to ensure you are using the discrete GPU.

On Linux the equivalent would be something alike this:

echo "blacklist i915" | sudo tee -a /etc/modprobe.d/blacklist.conf
reboot

Or disable the Intel GPU in the BIOS, when possible.

Q: Excel vba/macro file produces errors - cause: named ranges being copied? A:

I am not sure from the description whether the problem is with the xlsx file you create or the xlsm file you use to create the xlsx files or both.

For the xlsm file, try creating new sheets that are giving you problems, set new ranges in these sheets, and delete the old sheets.

If you have the worksheets with results in your xlsm file, then it is easy to create a blank workbook, copy your result worksheets to the new workbook, and then save the new workbook as an xlsx file. I believe named ranges would be copied into the new xlsx - you certainly shouldn't be getting any errors

Maybe some code examples would help me understand what actual problems you are seeing with the worksheets and the file creation. Following is the code I use to create an xlsx workbook from an xlsm masterfile. This works quickly and without problems for me. Note the code unprotects each sheet and standardises the font in the new xlsx file.

Dim newwb As Workbook
Dim Path As String
Path = Environ("Temp") & "\CollierPark\Backup\"
'Check to see if directory exists and if not then create it
Call MkDir_recursive(Path)
Dim FileName As String
FileName = "CPLog" & Format(playdate, "yyyymmdd")
Dim SheetNames ' array of sheets to write to new workbook
SheetNames = Array("HandiCapLog", "Handicaps", "WinLog", "BirdiesFerrets", "CompLog", "OtherWinners", "PlayLog", _
               "HCapList", "Var", "Names", "Results", "CurrentComp", "Champlog", "Today")
'Check to see if file exists
If Len(Dir(Path & FileName & ".xlsx")) <> 0 Then Kill (Path & FileName & ".xlsx")
'create new workbook
Application.DisplayAlerts = False
Application.ScreenUpdating = False
Worksheets(SheetNames).Copy
Dim sh As Worksheet
With ActiveWorkbook
   For Each sh In ActiveWorkbook.Worksheets
      sh.Visible = xlSheetVisible
      sh.Unprotect
      sh.Cells.Font.name = "Calibri"
      sh.Cells.Font.Size = 14
   Next
   .SaveAs FileName:=Path & FileName, FileFormat:=xlOpenXMLWorkbook
   .Close savechanges:=False
End With

Q: OpenStreetMap Building Identification Tags A:

Have a look at https://wiki.openstreetmap.org/wiki/Buildings.

building=yes is basically the default tagging, when the kind of building was unknown or simply not recorded at the time (for example, when aerial images are traced, where the kind of building isn't obvious). In OSM there is a "rule" that is better to tag incomplete information than not to tag at all.

The color of the buildings are determined by the value of the building tag. The surrounding areas are separate objects usually tagged with landuse.

If you need more complete information, then you have probably two options:

  1. Join the efforts of OSM and update the tagging yourself
  2. Find out if there are any official, possibly free data sets available from the City of New York (or the Borough of Brooklyn). A quick google pointed me to https://experience.arcgis.com/experience/d826b115c87841d491c2b41fcb175305 and https://www.nyc.gov/content/planning/pages/resources/datasets/mappluto-pluto-change, which may be suitable. (Important: Do not use these sources to update OSM. The licenses may not be compatible.)
